newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian ERM deal done in outline - minister.
newsitem.headline: Italian ERM deal done in outline - minister.

text.p: Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was quoted as saying on Saturday that agreement on the terms of the lira's return to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) already existed in outline.

A meeting of the EU's monetary committee has been called for 1200 GMT in Brussels on Saturday to decide the rate at which the lira should be allowed back into the currency grid after a four year absence.
"When the (monetary committee) meeting is called, the agreement in principle is already there," Ciampi was quoted as saying in an interview with Rome newspaper La Repubblica in an interview.
Ciampi said he could only recollect one instance where the monetary committee failed to strike a deal at a weekend meeting.
"It has only happened once, in 1983, for measures concerning France. That day we did not succeed in concluding the negotiation over the weekend," said Ciampi, a former Prime Minister.
Italy has said it is determined to take the lira back into the ERM to establish its credentials as prime contender to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.

Ciampi said he was involved in an abortive attempt to steer the lira back into the ERM in December 1992, only three months after it crashed out of the grid when a crisis of confidence over Italy's indebted finances sparked a run on the currency.
"I would have liked to re-enter at Christmas 1992," said Ciampi, who at the time was governor of the Bank of Italy.

Ciampi declined to say what would be an acceptable central parity level for the lira within the ERM but said that there were conflicting demands in France and Italy as to what the ideal rate would be.

"In the economic world of the two countries there are those who want it a bit higher and those who want it a bit lower," he said. "This corresponds to the interests and expectations of Italian and French operators that certainly don't work in the same direction," he added.

Italian newspapers plotted charts showing that, at one extreme, Italian employers would favour a parity level between the mark and the lira of 1,050 lire while France would be happy with a 950 lira parity .

A Reuters poll of 10 economists on Wednesday showed a majority expected a central parity rate of 1,000 against the mark. The lira would be allowed to fluctuate 15 percent either side of the central rate.
Several economists said the average exchange rate between the lira and mark over the past six months -- which works out at 1,010 lire -- could be used as a basis for an agreement.
The Finnish markka's entry into the currency grid last month was based on a six-month average rate against the German currency.
Economists have also speculated over whether the Bank of Italy would time a cut in interest rates to coincide with the lira's return to the ERM or whether it would prefer to wait.

Preliminary inflation figures for November released by Italian cities on Thursday and Friday signalled that Italian inflation may be set to fall to 2.6 percent year-on-year from three percent in October, smooth the path for an interest rate cut.
